description: Pubic-region phenotype: pubic hair distribution pattern, density, color, texture, and visible grooming state. Mons pubis prominence is captured in the corresponding vulva.json or penis.json suprapubic_fat_pad dimensions and is not duplicated here. The schema is published in the canonical vocabulary for academic transparency; observations from public-domain photographs are not populated and the file carries `observations_source_policy: "internal_only"`.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in dermatologic and endocrinologic literature on pubic-hair escutcheon morphology; Tanner staging (P1-P5) covers developmental progression but not adult escutcheon shape, which this dimension captures.
dimensions.description: Shape of the adult pubic hair distribution above and around the genitals. Sex-correlated (typically inverted-triangle in females, diamond extending up the midline in males) but with substantial individual variation including ethnic-correlated patterns.

values.definition: No terminal pubic hair; only vellus hair.
Limited terminal-hair presence; well below typical Tanner P5 density.
Inverted-triangle pattern with the base above the genitals; minimal extension up the abdominal midline. Tanner female P5.
Diamond-shape pattern with terminal hair extending up the abdominal midline toward the umbilicus. Tanner male P5.
Distribution extending laterally onto inner thigh / hip; common variant in some populations.
Small, sharply demarcated patch only; reduced from typical adult distribution.

observability.notes: Visibility heavily affected by grooming. The `pubic_grooming_style_visible` dimension should be assessed concurrently to interpret native distribution.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in dermatologic and endocrinologic literature; no single canonical scale beyond Tanner staging which addresses developmental progression rather than adult density variation.
dimensions.description: Density of native pubic hair when ungroomed.

values.definition: Visible terminal hairs scattered with substantial visible skin between.
Average density; terminal hairs cover most of the distribution area but with visible skin in between.
High terminal-hair count; minimal visible skin within the distribution.
Extremely high terminal-hair count; covers the entire distribution thickly.

observability.notes: Grooming substantially affects observed density; native density assessment requires ungroomed presentation.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in trichology literature; pubic hair color does not always match scalp hair color (commonly slightly darker; can be substantially different).
dimensions.description: Predominant color of native pubic hair.

values.definition: Color similar to scalp hair.
Pubic hair noticeably darker than scalp hair; common variant.
Pubic hair noticeably lighter than scalp hair; less common.
Mixed pigmented and gray hairs; common with aging.
Majority of hairs gray or white.

dimensions.scale_citation: Andre Walker hair-texture classification (1A-4C) was originally developed for scalp hair; pubic-hair texture descriptors aligned to that vocabulary by trichology and dermatology references.
dimensions.description: Texture of native pubic hair shafts. Pubic hair is typically curlier than scalp hair due to anatomical follicle orientation, but degree of curl varies by individual and population.

values.definition: No discernible curl; hair lies flat. Less common for pubic hair.
Loose S-curves; some body.
Tight S-curves to spiral curls; the typical pubic-hair pattern.
Tight coils or zig-zag pattern; common in Sub-Saharan African and African-diaspora populations.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with the descriptors used in survey-based pubic-grooming research (Herbenick D et al. 2017, Journal of Sexual Medicine).
dimensions.description: Visible grooming state — not a native phenotype dimension, but observability metadata that affects interpretation of every other dimension in this file. Captured here so that downstream analysis can flag native-phenotype dimensions as unreliable when grooming is detected.

values.definition: No visible grooming; native distribution and density observable.
Length reduced uniformly; distribution and density close to native but length altered.
Partial removal in a defined shape (e.g. landing strip, triangle); native distribution not directly observable.
Complete hair removal; no native phenotype observable from this presentation.
Image quality or framing prevents grooming-state assessment.

observability.notes: Grooming state is observability metadata, not a native phenotype dimension. When grooming is `shaped` or `fully_removed`, the other dimensions in this file should not be populated from the same photograph.

data_governance.rationale: Same as vulva.json and penis.json — schema published academically, observations require internal source-cleared sources only.

references: Marshall WA, Tanner JM (1969). Variations in pattern of pubertal changes in girls. Archives of Disease in Childhood, 44(235): 291-303.
Marshall WA, Tanner JM (1970). Variations in the pattern of pubertal changes in boys. Archives of Disease in Childhood, 45(239): 13-23.
Herbenick D, Schick V, Reece M, Sanders SA, Fortenberry JD (2010). Pubic hair removal among women in the United States: prevalence, methods, and characteristics. Journal of Sexual Medicine, 7(10).

Herbenick D, Hensel D, Smith NK, Schick V, Reece M, Sanders SA, Fortenberry JD (2017). Pubic hair removal and sexual behavior: findings from a prospective daily diary study of sexually active women in the United States. Journal of Sexual Medicine, 14(8).
